keyFindings.description: On an unreadable lock the disk watcher returns: it records nothing, stops nothing and never watches again for the rest of the step, so load keeps arriving while Postgres fills the volume, breaking the guard's own contract. A failed read says nothing about whose copy it is; the watcher should restore its TERM trap and poll again. runner_wait's deadline stop has the same shape (1586-1588).

copy_is_ours reads with 2>/dev/null, so kubectl's error (forbidden, refused, timeout) is lost and the fail-closed note cannot say why a run stopped; it is also a second retry loop beside kube_read. Keep the last try's stderr in the note, or read through kube_read.
postgres_exec and runner_exec carry the same -t/-i parse, which only works in that order; one copy_exec helper.
liveSummary.Transport has no omitempty, so every new summary.json writes "transport": "" though the comment says it is never written.
